issue.title: sase-nvim lsp_vcs_project_smoke: '+s' plus-tag completion inserts a leading newline ('\n+sase ' instead of '+sase ')

task_type_fields.why_not_flake:
Proposed by sase-1eq.9 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #1, then attributed to installed-server drift against sase-xprompt-lsp 0.36.4). The sase-1eq land agent re-ran it on 2026-10-05 against sase-macro-lsp 0.36.5 built from the pinned sase-core fe2ef0e6, at sase-nvim 09d8187. Of the five smokes in that proposal, project_tag_highlight, artifact_ref, and vcs_ref now pass. model_shortcut fails for the star-to-equals migration and is recorded on epic sase-z3. This smoke still fails deterministically on its first assertion:

    expansion mismatch for '+s'
      expected: "+sase "
      actual:   "\n+sase "

Repro, from the sase-nvim checkout:
SASE_MACRO_LSP_CMD=<sase venv>/bin/sase-macro-lsp nvim --headless -u NONE -c 'set rtp+=.' -c "lua print(pcall(dofile,'tests/lsp_vcs_project_smoke.lua'))" -c 'qa!'

The applied completion inserts a leading newline before the expanded "+sase " project tag. Either the LSP textEdit range or the plugin's plus-tag expansion path mishandles the single empty line the fixture writes, or the smoke's buffer-read assertion is stale. The root cause is not yet narrowed. The rest of the file's assertions (lines 287-301: "+ship", trailing "+" after prose, "#git:" and "#gh!!:" prefixes) never run while this one fails.

issue.creation_reason: A sase-nvim headless LSP smoke has been red since at least 2026-10-03 and still fails against the current pinned macro LSP, so the editor's plus-tag project completion path is unverified. Proposed by sase-1eq.9 and re-reproduced by the sase-1eq land agent.
